passages.text: Then Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and power to cure diseases.
passages.sermon:
Jesus called His twelve disciples together.
Jesus gave the twelve disciples power.
Jesus gave them authority over all demons.
Jesus gave them power to cure diseases.
passages.original: Συνκαλεσάμενος δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δύναμιν καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ νόσους θεραπεύειν

passages.text: And He sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
passages.sermon:
Jesus called the Twelve disciples together.
Jesus gave them power and authority over all demons.
Jesus gave them power to cure diseases.
Jesus sent the Twelve disciples out.
He told them to proclaim the kingdom of God.
He told them to heal the sick.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἰᾶσθαι τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς

passages.text: “Take nothing for the journey,” He told them, “no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, no second tunic.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Twelve disciples.
He gave them instructions for their journey.
He said, “Take nothing with you for the journey.
Do not take a staff.
Do not take a bag.
Do not take bread.
Do not take money.
Do not take a second tunic.”
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Μηδὲν αἴρετε εἰς τὴν ὁδόν μήτε ῥάβδον μήτε πήραν μήτε ἄρτον μήτε ἀργύριον μήτε ἀνὰ δύο χιτῶνας ἔχειν

passages.text: Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that area.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He gave them instructions for their journey.
He said, “When you enter a house, stay in that house.
Remain there until you leave that place.”
passages.original: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν οἰκίαν εἰσέλθητε ἐκεῖ μένετε καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἐξέρχεσθε

passages.text: If anyone does not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He gave them instructions for their journey.
He said, “If anyone does not welcome you, leave that town.
When you leave, shake the dust off your feet.
This act will be a testimony against those people.”
passages.original: καὶ ὅσοι ἂν μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς ἐξερχόμενοι ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης τὸν κονιορτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν ἀποτινάσσετε εἰς μαρτύριον ἐπ’ αὐτούς

passages.text: So they set out and went from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing people everywhere.
passages.sermon:
The apostles went out.
They traveled from village to village.
They preached the gospel in each place.
They healed people everywhere they went.
passages.original: Ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ διήρχοντο κατὰ τὰς κώμας εὐαγγελιζόμενοι καὶ θεραπεύοντες πανταχοῦ

passages.text: When Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, he was perplexed. For some were saying that John had risen from the dead, others that Elijah had appeared, and still others that a prophet of old had arisen.
passages.sermon:
Herod was the tetrarch.
Herod heard about everything that was happening.
Herod felt confused.
Some people said, “John has risen from the dead.”
Other people said, “Elijah has appeared.”
Still other people said, “A prophet from long ago has come back to life.”
passages.original: Ἤκουσεν δὲ Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὰ γινόμενα πάντα καὶ διηπόρει διὰ τὸ λέγεσθαι ὑπό τινων ὅτι Ἰωάννης ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν ὑπό τινων δὲ ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐφάνη ἄλλων δὲ ὅτι προφήτης τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη

passages.text: “I beheaded John,” Herod said, “but who is this man I hear such things about?” And he kept trying to see Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Herod was the tetrarch.
Herod said, "I beheaded John."
Herod heard many things about another man.
Herod asked, "Who is this man I hear such things about?"
Herod kept trying to see Jesus.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης Ἰωάννην ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα τίς δέ ἐστιν οὗτος περὶ οὗ ἀκούω τοιαῦτα καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν αὐτόν

passages.text: Then the apostles returned and reported to Jesus all that they had done. Taking them away privately, He withdrew to a town called Bethsaida.
passages.sermon:
The apostles returned to Jesus.
The apostles told Jesus everything they had done.
Jesus took the apostles with Him.
Jesus led them away from the crowds.
Jesus went with them to a town called Bethsaida.
passages.original: Καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες οἱ ἀπόστολοι διηγήσαντο αὐτῷ ὅσα ἐποίησαν Καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ὑπεχώρησεν κατ’ ἰδίαν εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Βηθσαϊδά

passages.text: But the crowds found out and followed Him. He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and He healed those who needed healing.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in Bethsaida.
Many people learned where Jesus was.
The crowds followed Jesus.
Jesus welcomed the crowds.
Jesus spoke to the crowds about the kingdom of God.
Some people in the crowd needed healing.
Jesus healed those who needed healing.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι γνόντες ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ καὶ ἀποδεξάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς χρείαν ἔχοντας θεραπείας ἰᾶτο

passages.text: As the day neared its end, the Twelve came to Jesus and said, “Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding villages and countryside for lodging and provisions. For we are in a desolate place here.”
passages.sermon:
The day began to end.
The Twelve disciples came to Jesus.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Send the crowd away.”
They said, “Let them go to the nearby villages and countryside.”
They said, “There they can find a place to stay.”
They said, “There they can find food.”
They said, “We are in a deserted place here.”
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤρξατο κλίνειν προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δώδεκα εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ἀπόλυσον τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα πορευθέντες εἰς τὰς κύκλῳ κώμας καὶ ἀγροὺς καταλύσωσιν καὶ εὕρωσιν ἐπισιτισμόν ὅτι ὧδε ἐν ἐρήμῳ τόπῳ ἐσμέν

passages.text: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” “We have only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered, “unless we go and buy food for all these people.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “You give them something to eat.”
The disciples answered Jesus.
They said, “We have only five loaves of bread and two fish.”
They also said, “We would have to go and buy food for all these people.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Δότε αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν ὑμεῖς Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Οὐκ εἰσὶν ἡμῖν πλεῖον ἢ ἄρτοι πέντε καὶ ἰχθύες δύο εἰ μήτι πορευθέντες ἡμεῖς ἀγοράσωμεν εἰς πάντα τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον βρώματα

passages.text: (There were about five thousand men.) He told His disciples, “Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with a large crowd.
There were about five thousand men present.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them to organize the people.
He said, “Have them sit down in groups.”
Each group should have about fifty people.
passages.original: ἦσαν γὰρ ὡσεὶ ἄνδρες πεντακισχίλιοι Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ Κατακλίνατε αὐτοὺς κλισίας ὡσεὶ ἀνὰ πεντήκοντα

passages.text: They did so, and everyone was seated.
passages.sermon: The disciples obeyed Jesus.\r\nThey seated everyone.\r\nAll the people sat down.
passages.original: καὶ ἐποίησαν οὕτως καὶ κατέκλιναν ἅπαντας

passages.text: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke them. Then He gave them to the disciples to set before the people.
passages.sermon:
Jesus took five loaves of bread.
He also took two fish.
Jesus looked up to heaven.
He spoke a blessing over the bread and fish.
Jesus broke the bread and fish into pieces.
He gave the pieces to His disciples.
The disciples set the food before the people.
passages.original: Λαβὼν δὲ τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ κατέκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς παραθεῖναι τῷ ὄχλῳ

passages.text: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had just blessed and broken the five loaves and two fish.
The disciples gave the food to the people.
Everyone ate.
Everyone was satisfied.
The disciples collected what was left over.
They picked up twelve baskets full of broken pieces.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν πάντες καὶ ἤρθη τὸ περισσεῦσαν αὐτοῖς κλασμάτων κόφινοι δώδεκα

passages.text: One day as Jesus was praying in private and the disciples were with Him, He questioned them: “Who do the crowds say I am?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was praying alone.
His disciples were with Him.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Who do the crowds say I am?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν προσευχόμενον κατὰ μόνας συνῆσαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς λέγων Τίνα με οἱ ὄχλοι λέγουσιν εἶναι

passages.text: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, that a prophet of old has arisen.”
passages.sermon:
The disciples answered Jesus.
Some people say you are John the Baptist.
Other people say you are Elijah.
Still other people say you are a prophet from long ago who has come back to life.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν Ἰωάννην τὸν Βαπτιστήν ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν ἄλλοι δὲ ὅτι προφήτης τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη

passages.text: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
Jesus said, "But what about you?"
He said, "Who do you say I am?"
Peter answered Jesus.
Peter said, "You are the Christ of God."
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι Πέτρος δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Τὸν Χριστὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Jesus strictly warned them not to tell this to anyone.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nJesus gave them a strict warning.\r\nHe told them not to tell anyone this.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐπιτιμήσας αὐτοῖς παρήγγειλεν μηδενὶ λέγειν τοῦτο

passages.text: “The Son of Man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus called Himself the Son of Man.
Jesus said the Son of Man must suffer many things.
The elders will reject the Son of Man.
The chief priests will reject the Son of Man.
The scribes will reject the Son of Man.
They will kill the Son of Man.
On the third day, God will raise the Son of Man to life.
passages.original: εἰπὼν ὅτι Δεῖ τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθῆναι

passages.text: Then Jesus said to all of them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to everyone.
Jesus said, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself.
He must take up his cross every day.
He must follow Me.”
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς πάντας Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἔρχεσθαι ἀρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καθ’ ἡμέραν καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι

passages.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nHe said, “Whoever wants to save his own life will lose it.\r\nBut whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.”
passages.original: ὃς γὰρ ἂν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ οὗτος σώσει αὐτήν

passages.text: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or forfeit his very self?
passages.sermon:
A man may gain the whole world.
He may become rich and powerful.
He may have everything the world offers.
But if he loses himself, he gains nothing.
If he ruins his own life, he suffers great loss.
Gaining the world does not help if a man loses his true self.
passages.original: Τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖται ἄνθρωπος κερδήσας τὸν κόσμον ὅλον ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἀπολέσας ἢ ζημιωθείς

passages.text: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when He comes in His glory and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
If any person feels ashamed of Jesus,
If any person feels ashamed of the words of Jesus,
The Son of Man will feel ashamed of that person.
This will happen when the Son of Man comes in His glory.
He will come in the glory of the Father.
He will come with the holy angels.
passages.original: ὃς γὰρ ἂν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους τοῦτον ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων

passages.text: But I tell you truthfully, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people who were with Him.
He said something true.
Some people who stand here will not die yet.
They will see the kingdom of God before they die.
passages.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ἀληθῶς εἰσίν τινες τῶν αὐτοῦ ἑστηκότων οἳ οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: About eight days after Jesus had said these things, He took with Him Peter, John, and James, and went up on a mountain to pray.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus spoke important words to His disciples.
About eight days after Jesus spoke these words, He acted.
Jesus took Peter, John, and James with Him.
Jesus led Peter, John, and James up a mountain.
Jesus went up the mountain to pray.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὡσεὶ ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ καὶ παραλαβὼν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι

passages.text: And as He was praying, the appearance of His face changed, and His clothes became radiantly white.
passages.sermon:
Jesus went up on a mountain to pray.
He prayed.
As Jesus prayed, His face changed.
His appearance became different.
His clothes became white.
His clothes shone with brightness.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ προσεύχεσθαι αὐτὸν τὸ εἶδος τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἕτερον καὶ ὁ ἱματισμὸς αὐτοῦ λευκὸς ἐξαστράπτων

passages.text: Suddenly two men, Moses and Elijah, began talking with Jesus.
passages.sermon: Two men appeared.\r\nTheir names were Moses and Elijah.\r\nThey began talking with Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο συνελάλουν αὐτῷ οἵτινες ἦσαν Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας

passages.text: They appeared in glory and spoke about His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Moses and Elijah appeared.
They appeared in glory.
They spoke with Jesus.
They spoke about His departure.
Jesus was about to accomplish His departure at Jerusalem.
passages.original: οἳ ὀφθέντες ἐν δόξῃ ἔλεγον τὴν ἔξοδον αὐτοῦ ἣν ἤμελλεν πληροῦν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: Meanwhile Peter and his companions were overcome by sleep, but when they awoke, they saw Jesus’ glory and the two men standing with Him.
passages.sermon:
Peter was with his companions.
They became very sleepy.
They fell asleep.
Later, they woke up.
They saw Jesus’ glory.
They saw two men standing with Jesus.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ ἦσαν βεβαρημένοι ὕπνῳ διαγρηγορήσαντες δὲ εἶδον τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς δύο ἄνδρας τοὺς συνεστῶτας αὐτῷ

passages.text: As Moses and Elijah were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters —one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” (He did not know what he was saying.)
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Moses and Elijah were leaving Jesus.
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter said, “Master, it is good for us to be here.”
Peter said, “Let us put up three shelters.”
Peter said, “One shelter will be for You.”
Peter said, “One shelter will be for Moses.”
Peter said, “One shelter will be for Elijah.”
Peter did not know what he was saying.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ διαχωρίζεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν Ἐπιστάτα καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι καὶ ποιήσωμεν σκηνὰς τρεῖς μίαν σοὶ καὶ μίαν Μωϋσεῖ καὶ μίαν Ἠλίᾳ μὴ εἰδὼς ὃ λέγει

passages.text: While Peter was speaking, a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
passages.sermon:
Peter was speaking.
A cloud appeared.
The cloud covered Peter, Jesus, James, and John.
They entered the cloud.
They became afraid.
passages.original: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ἐγένετο νεφέλη καὶ ἐπεσκίαζεν αὐτούς ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ ἐν τῷ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν νεφέλην

passages.text: And a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!”
passages.sermon:
A voice spoke from the cloud.
The voice said, “This is My Son.”
God chose Jesus.
God said, “Listen to Him.”
passages.original: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ ἐκλελεγμένος αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε

passages.text: After the voice had spoken, only Jesus was present with them. The disciples kept this to themselves, and in those days they did not tell anyone what they had seen.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus stood alone with the disciples after the voice spoke.
The disciples stayed silent.
The disciples did not tell anyone what they had seen during those days.
passages.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ γενέσθαι τὴν φωνὴν εὑρέθη Ἰησοῦς μόνος καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐσίγησαν καὶ οὐδενὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις οὐδὲν ὧν ἑώρακαν

passages.text: The next day, when they came down from the mountain, Jesus was met by a large crowd.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
God chose Jesus.
The next day, Jesus and His disciples came down from the mountain.
A large crowd met Jesus.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ τῇ ἑξῆς ἡμέρᾳ κατελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄρους συνήντησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς

passages.text: Suddenly a man in the crowd cried out, “Teacher, I beg You to look at my son, for he is my only child.
passages.sermon:
A man stood in the crowd.
He cried out suddenly.
He spoke to Jesus.
He called Jesus “Teacher.”
He begged Jesus to look at his son.
He said, “He is my only child.”
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ἐβόησεν λέγων Διδάσκαλε δέομαί σου ἐπιβλέψαι ἐπὶ τὸν υἱόν μου ὅτι μονογενής μοί ἐστιν

passages.text: A spirit keeps seizing him, and he screams abruptly. It throws him into convulsions so that he foams at the mouth. It keeps mauling him and rarely departs from him.
passages.sermon:
A spirit attacks my son.
The spirit suddenly seizes him.
He screams loudly.
The spirit throws him into convulsions.
He foams at the mouth.
The spirit hurts him badly.
The spirit rarely leaves him.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ πνεῦμα λαμβάνει αὐτόν καὶ ἐξαίφνης κράζει καὶ σπαράσσει αὐτὸν μετὰ ἀφροῦ καὶ μόγις ἀποχωρεῖ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ συντρῖβον αὐτόν

passages.text: I begged Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.”
passages.sermon: A man from the crowd spoke to Jesus.\r\nHe said, “I begged Your disciples to drive out the spirit from my son.\r\nThey could not do it.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐδεήθην τῶν μαθητῶν σου ἵνα ἐκβάλωσιν αὐτό καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν

passages.text: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you and put up with you? Bring your son here.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He called them an unbelieving and perverse generation.
He asked, “How long must I stay with you?”
He asked, “How long must I put up with you?”
He said, “Bring your son here.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη ἕως πότε ἔσομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν προσάγαγε ὧδε τὸν υἱόν σου

passages.text: Even while the boy was approaching, the demon slammed him to the ground in a convulsion. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
A boy was coming toward Jesus.
An unclean spirit possessed the boy.
The demon threw the boy to the ground.
The boy had a convulsion.
Jesus spoke to the unclean spirit.
Jesus rebuked the spirit.
Jesus healed the boy.
Jesus gave the boy back to his father.
passages.original: Ἔτι δὲ προσερχομένου αὐτοῦ ἔρρηξεν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον καὶ συνεσπάραξεν ἐπετίμησεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ καὶ ἰάσατο τὸν παῖδα καὶ ἀπέδωκεν αὐτὸν τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And they were all astonished at the greatness of God. While everyone was marveling at all that Jesus was doing, He said to His disciples, “Let these words sink into your ears: The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.”
passages.sermon:
Everyone saw what happened.
Everyone felt amazed at God's greatness.
People watched Jesus.
People marveled at everything Jesus did.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “Listen carefully to my words.”
Jesus said, “The Son of Man will soon be handed over to men.”
passages.original: Ἐξεπλήσσοντο δὲ πάντες ἐπὶ τῇ μεγαλειότητι τοῦ Θεοῦ Πάντων δὲ θαυμαζόντων ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐποίει εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ Θέσθε ὑμεῖς εἰς τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὁ γὰρ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: But they did not understand this statement. It was veiled from them so that they could not comprehend it, and they were afraid to ask Him about it.
passages.sermon:
The disciples did not understand what Jesus said.
God kept the meaning hidden from them.
They could not grasp what Jesus meant.
They felt afraid to ask Jesus about His words.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο καὶ ἦν παρακεκαλυμμένον ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἵνα μὴ αἴσθωνται αὐτό καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο ἐρωτῆσαι αὐτὸν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος τούτου

passages.text: Then an argument started among the disciples as to which of them would be the greatest.
passages.sermon:
The disciples followed Jesus.
The disciples began to argue.
They argued with each other.
They wanted to know who would be the greatest among them.
passages.original: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ διαλογισμὸς ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸ τίς ἂν εἴη μείζων αὐτῶν

passages.text: But Jesus, knowing the thoughts of their hearts, had a little child stand beside Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus knew what the disciples were thinking in their hearts.\r\nHe took a little child.\r\nHe placed the child beside Himself.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἰδὼς τὸν διαλογισμὸν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενος παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ παρ’ ἑαυτῷ

passages.text: And He said to them, “Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me. For whoever is the least among all of you, he is the greatest.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me.
Whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me.
The One who sent Me is God the Father.
Whoever is the least among all of you is the greatest.”
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὃς ἐὰν δέξηται τοῦτο τὸ παιδίον ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ἐμὲ δέχεται καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐμὲ δέξηται δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με ὁ γὰρ μικρότερος ἐν πᾶσιν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχων οὗτός ἐστιν μέγας

passages.text: “Master,” said John, “we saw someone driving out demons in Your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us.”
passages.sermon:
John spoke to Jesus.
John called Jesus “Master.”
John said, “We saw someone.”
This person was driving out demons.
He was using Your name, Jesus.
We tried to stop him.
We did this because he does not go with us.
He does not follow us.
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰωάννης εἶπεν Ἐπιστάτα εἴδομέν τινα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια καὶ ἐκωλύομεν αὐτὸν ὅτι οὐκ ἀκολουθεῖ μεθ’ ἡμῶν

passages.text: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied, “for whoever is not against you is for you.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to John.\r\nJesus said, “Do not stop him.”\r\nAnyone who is not against you is for you.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μὴ κωλύετε ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθ’ ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐστιν

passages.text: As the day of His ascension approached, Jesus resolutely set out for Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
The day of His ascension was coming soon.
Jesus knew this time was near.
He made a firm decision.
He set His face toward Jerusalem.
He began to go to Jerusalem.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ἀναλήμψεως αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς τὸ πρόσωπον ἐστήρισεν τοῦ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: He sent messengers on ahead, who went into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was traveling to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead of Him.
The messengers went into a Samaritan village.
They went to prepare for Jesus’ arrival.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν ἀγγέλους πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ καὶ πορευθέντες εἰσῆλθον εἰς κώμην Σαμαριτῶν ὡς ἑτοιμάσαι αὐτῷ

passages.text: But the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem.
passages.sermon: The people in that Samaritan village saw Jesus.\r\nThey knew He was traveling to Jerusalem.\r\nThey refused to welcome Him.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἐδέξαντο αὐτόν ὅτι τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἦν πορευόμενον εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: When the disciples James and John saw this, they asked, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?”
passages.sermon:
James and John were disciples of Jesus.
They saw that the people in the Samaritan village refused to welcome Jesus.
James and John spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Lord, do you want us to call down fire from heaven?”
They asked if they should destroy those people with fire.
passages.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης εἶπαν Κύριε θέλεις εἴπωμεν πῦρ καταβῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀναλῶσαι αὐτούς

passages.text: But Jesus turned and rebuked them.
passages.sermon: Jesus turned to James and John.\r\nHe rebuked them.
passages.original: Στραφεὶς δὲ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: And He and His disciples went on to another village.
passages.sermon: Jesus led His disciples.\r\nThey left the place where they were.\r\nThey traveled to a different village.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς ἑτέραν κώμην

passages.text: As they were walking along the road, someone said to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.”
passages.sermon: Jesus walked with His disciples along the road.\r\nA man spoke to Jesus.\r\nThe man said, “I will follow You wherever You go.”
passages.original: Καὶ πορευομένων αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπέν τις πρὸς αὐτόν Ἀκολουθήσω σοι ὅπου ἐὰν ἀπέρχῃ

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Foxes have dens.
Birds of the air have nests.
The Son of Man has no place to lay His head.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Αἱ ἀλώπεκες φωλεοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνώσεις ὁ δὲ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνῃ

passages.text: Then He said to another man, “Follow Me.” The man replied, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to another man.
Jesus said, “Follow Me.”
The man answered Jesus.
The man said, “Lord, let me go first.”
The man said, “Let me bury my father.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς ἕτερον Ἀκολούθει μοι ὁ Δὲ εἶπεν Κύριε Ἐπίτρεψόν μοι πρῶτον ἀπελθόντι θάψαι τὸν πατέρα μου

passages.text: But Jesus told him, “Let the dead bury their own dead. You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus said, “Let the dead bury their own dead.”
Jesus commanded the man to go.
Jesus told the man to proclaim the kingdom of God.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ Ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς σὺ δὲ ἀπελθὼν διάγγελλε τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Still another said, “I will follow You, Lord; but first let me bid farewell to my family.”
passages.sermon: A man spoke to Jesus.\r\nHe said, “Lord, I will follow You.”\r\nHe also said, “First, let me say goodbye to my family at home.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ ἕτερος Ἀκολουθήσω σοι Κύριε πρῶτον δὲ ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ἀποτάξασθαι τοῖς εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου

passages.text: Then Jesus declared, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to him.
Jesus said this to a man who wanted to follow Him but wanted to say goodbye to his family first.
Jesus said, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
A person who starts working for God’s kingdom must not turn back.
Anyone who looks back after beginning is not ready for God’s kingdom.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐδεὶς ἐπιβαλὼν τὴν χεῖρα ἐπ’ ἄροτρον καὶ βλέπων εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω εὔθετός ἐστιν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ
